paragraphs.text: translated by
1. I PRAISE your Charioteer of sacrifice, the Lord of men, Priest of the tribes, refulgent, Guest of night.
paragraphs.original: यज्ञस्य वो रथ्यं विश्पतिं विशां होतारमक्तोरतिथिं विभावसुम् ।
paragraphs.translit: yajñasya vo rathyaṃ viśpatiṃ viśāṃ hotāramaktoratithiṃ vibhāvasum |

paragraphs.text: Blazing amid dry plants, snatching amid the green, the Strong, the Holy Herald hath attained to heaven.
paragraphs.original: शोचञ्छुष्कासु हरिणीषु जर्भुरद्वृषा केतुर्यजतो द्यामशायत
paragraphs.translit: śocañchuṣkāsu hariṇīṣu jarbhuradvṛṣā keturyajato dyāmaśāyata

paragraphs.text: 2. Him, Agni, Gods and men have made their chief support, who drinks the fatness and completes the sacrifice.
paragraphs.original: इममञ्जस्पामुभये अकृण्वत धर्माणमग्निं विदथस्य साधनम् ।
paragraphs.translit: imamañjaspāmubhaye akṛṇvata dharmāṇamagniṃ vidathasya sādhanam |

paragraphs.text: With kisses they caress the Grandson of the Red, like the swift ray of light, the Household Priest of Dawn.
paragraphs.original: अक्तुं न यह्वमुषसः पुरोहितं तनूनपातमरुषस्य निंसते
paragraphs.translit: aktuṃ na yahvamuṣasaḥ purohitaṃ tanūnapātamaruṣasya niṃsate

paragraphs.text: 3. Yea, we discriminate his and the niggard's ways: his branches evermore are sent forth to consume.
paragraphs.original: बळस्य नीथा वि पणेश्च मन्महे वया अस्य प्रहुता आसुरत्तवे ।
paragraphs.translit: baḷasya nīthā vi paṇeśca manmahe vayā asya prahutā āsurattave |

paragraphs.text: When his terrific flames have reached the Immortal's world, then men remember and extol the Heavenly Folk.
paragraphs.original: यदा घोरासो अमृतत्वमाशतादिज्जनस्य दैव्यस्य चर्किरन्
paragraphs.translit: yadā ghorāso amṛtatvamāśatādijjanasya daivyasya carkiran

paragraphs.text: 4. For then the net of Law, Dyaus, and the wide expanse, Earth, Worship, and Devotion meet for highest praise,
paragraphs.original: ऋतस्य हि प्रसितिर्द्यौरुरु व्यचो नमो मह्यरमतिः पनीयसी ।
paragraphs.translit: ṛtasya hi prasitirdyaururu vyaco namo mahyaramatiḥ panīyasī |

paragraphs.text: Varuna, Indra, Mitra were of one accord, and Savitar and Bhaga, Lords of holy might.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रो मित्रो वरुणः सं चिकित्रिरेऽथो भगः सविता पूतदक्षसः
paragraphs.translit: indro mitro varuṇaḥ saṃ cikitrire'tho bhagaḥ savitā pūtadakṣasaḥ

paragraphs.text: 5. Onward, with ever-roaming Rudra, speed the floods: over Aramati the Mighty have they run.
paragraphs.original: प्र रुद्रेण ययिना यन्ति सिन्धवस्तिरो महीमरमतिं दधन्विरे ।
paragraphs.translit: pra rudreṇa yayinā yanti sindhavastiro mahīmaramatiṃ dadhanvire |

paragraphs.text: With them Parijman, moving round his vast domain, loud bellowing, bedews all things that are within.
paragraphs.original: येभिः परिज्मा परियन्नुरु ज्रयो वि रोरुवज्जठरे विश्वमुक्षते
paragraphs.translit: yebhiḥ parijmā pariyannuru jrayo vi roruvajjaṭhare viśvamukṣate

paragraphs.text: 6. Straightway the Rudras, Maruts visiting all men, Falcons of Dyaus, home-dwellers with the Asura,-
paragraphs.original: क्राणा रुद्रा मरुतो विश्वकृष्टयो दिवः श्येनासो असुरस्य नीळयः ।
paragraphs.translit: krāṇā rudrā maruto viśvakṛṣṭayo divaḥ śyenāso asurasya nīḷayaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman look on with these, and the swift-moving Indra with swift-moving Gods.
paragraphs.original: तेभिश्चष्टे वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमेन्द्रो देवेभिरर्वशेभिरर्वशः
paragraphs.translit: tebhiścaṣṭe varuṇo mitro aryamendro devebhirarvaśebhirarvaśaḥ

paragraphs.text: 7. With Indra have they found enjoyment, they who toil, in the light's beauty, in the very Strong One's strength;
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रे भुजं शशमानास आशत सूरो दृशीके वृषणश्च पौंस्ये ।
paragraphs.translit: indre bhujaṃ śaśamānāsa āśata sūro dṛśīke vṛṣaṇaśca pauṃsye |

paragraphs.text: The singers who in men's assemblies forged for him, according to his due, his friend the thunderbolt.
paragraphs.original: प्र ये न्वस्यार्हणा ततक्षिरे युजं वज्रं नृषदनेषु कारवः
paragraphs.translit: pra ye nvasyārhaṇā tatakṣire yujaṃ vajraṃ nṛṣadaneṣu kāravaḥ

paragraphs.text: 8. Even the Sun's Bay Coursers hath lie held in check: each one fears Indra as the mightiest of all.
paragraphs.original: सूरश्चिदा हरितो अस्य रीरमदिन्द्रादा कश्चिद्भयते तवीयसः ।
paragraphs.translit: sūraścidā harito asya rīramadindrādā kaścidbhayate tavīyasaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Unhindered, from the air's vault thunders day by day the loud triumphant breathing of the fearful Bull.
paragraphs.original: भीमस्य वृष्णो जठरादभिश्वसो दिवेदिवे सहुरि स्तन्नबाधितः
paragraphs.translit: bhīmasya vṛṣṇo jaṭharādabhiśvaso divedive sahuri stannabādhitaḥ

paragraphs.text: 9. With humble adoration show this day your song of praise to mighty Rudra, Ruler of the brave:
paragraphs.original: स्तोमं वो अद्य रुद्राय शिक्वसे क्षयद्वीराय नमसा दिदिष्टन ।
paragraphs.translit: stomaṃ vo adya rudrāya śikvase kṣayadvīrāya namasā didiṣṭana |

paragraphs.text: With whom, the Eager Ones, going their ordered course, he comes from heaven Self-bright, auspicious, strong to guard.
paragraphs.original: येभिः शिवः स्ववाँ एवयावभिर्दिवः सिषक्ति स्वयशा निकामभिः
paragraphs.translit: yebhiḥ śivaḥ svavām̐ evayāvabhirdivaḥ siṣakti svayaśā nikāmabhiḥ

paragraphs.text: 10. For these have spread abroad the fame of human kind, the Bull Brhaspati and Soma's brotherhood.
paragraphs.original: ते हि प्रजाया अभरन्त वि श्रवो बृहस्पतिर्वृषभः सोमजामयः ।
paragraphs.translit: te hi prajāyā abharanta vi śravo bṛhaspatirvṛṣabhaḥ somajāmayaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Atharvan first by sacrifices made men sure: through skill the Bhrgus were esteemed of all as Gods.
paragraphs.original: यज्ञैरथर्वा प्रथमो वि धारयद्देवा दक्षैर्भृगवः सं चिकित्रिरे
paragraphs.translit: yajñairatharvā prathamo vi dhārayaddevā dakṣairbhṛgavaḥ saṃ cikitrire

paragraphs.text: 11. For these, the Earth and Heaven with their abundant seed, four-bodied Narasmsa, Yama, Aditi,
paragraphs.original: ते हि द्यावापृथिवी भूरिरेतसा नराशंसश्चतुरङ्गो यमोऽदितिः ।
paragraphs.translit: te hi dyāvāpṛthivī bhūriretasā narāśaṃsaścaturaṅgo yamo'ditiḥ |

paragraphs.text: God Tvastar Wealth-bestower, the Rbhuksanas, Rodasi, Maruts, Visnu, claim and merit praise.
paragraphs.original: देवस्त्वष्टा द्रविणोदा ऋभुक्षणः प्र रोदसी मरुतो विष्णुरर्हिरे
paragraphs.translit: devastvaṣṭā draviṇodā ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ pra rodasī maruto viṣṇurarhire

paragraphs.text: 12. And may he too give car, the Sage, from far away, the Dragon of the Deep, to this our yearning call.
paragraphs.original: उत स्य न उशिजामुर्विया कविरहिः शृणोतु बुध्न्यो हवीमनि ।
paragraphs.translit: uta sya na uśijāmurviyā kavirahiḥ śṛṇotu budhnyo havīmani |

paragraphs.text: Ye Sun and Moon who dwell in heaven and move in turn, and with your thought, O Earth and Sky, observe this well.
paragraphs.original: सूर्यामासा विचरन्ता दिविक्षिता धिया शमीनहुषी अस्य बोधतम्
paragraphs.translit: sūryāmāsā vicarantā divikṣitā dhiyā śamīnahuṣī asya bodhatam

paragraphs.text: 13. Dear to all Gods, may Pasan guard the ways we go, the Waters' child and Vayu help us to success.
paragraphs.original: प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये ।
paragraphs.translit: pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye |

paragraphs.text: Sing lauds for your great bliss to Wind, the breath of all: ye Asvins prompt to hear, hear this upon your way.
paragraphs.original: आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतम्
paragraphs.translit: ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutam

paragraphs.text: 14. With hymns of praise we sing him who is throned as Lord over these fearless tribes, the Self-resplendent One.
paragraphs.original: विशामासामभयानामधिक्षितं गीर्भिरु स्वयशसं गृणीमसि ।
paragraphs.translit: viśāmāsāmabhayānāmadhikṣitaṃ gīrbhiru svayaśasaṃ gṛṇīmasi |

paragraphs.text: We praise Night's youthful Lord benevolent to men, the foeless One, the free, with all celestial Dames.
paragraphs.original: ग्नाभिर्विश्वाभिरदितिमनर्वणमक्तोर्युवानं नृमणा अधा पतिम्
paragraphs.translit: gnābhirviśvābhiraditimanarvaṇamaktoryuvānaṃ nṛmaṇā adhā patim

paragraphs.text: 15. By reason of his birth here Angiras first sang: the pressing-stones upraised beheld the sacrifice-
paragraphs.original: रेभदत्र जनुषा पूर्वो अङ्गिरा ग्रावाण ऊर्ध्वा अभि चक्षुरध्वरम् ।
paragraphs.translit: rebhadatra januṣā pūrvo aṅgirā grāvāṇa ūrdhvā abhi cakṣuradhvaram |

paragraphs.text: The stones through which the Sage became exceeding vast, and the sharp axe obtains in fight the beauteous place.
paragraphs.original: येभिर्विहाया अभवद्विचक्षणः पाथः सुमेकं स्वधितिर्वनन्वति
paragraphs.translit: yebhirvihāyā abhavadvicakṣaṇaḥ pāthaḥ sumekaṃ svadhitirvananvati
